AD-TIFROMs are a new family of TF-BSS methods, which are very efficient and accurate, and which are able to handle a large variety of source signals, including those with very low or very high TF sparsity, and those with a high overlap.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first TF-BSS algorithms for AD mixtures, and that they are suited to a large range of source characteristics.
we propose a novel TF-BSS approach, based on TF ratio of mixtures, which is suited to AD mixtures and which is especially efficient when applied in constant-time zones.
we have developed a new class of methods that can separate non-stationary and sparse sources, with no constraints on their sparsity or overlap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TF-Ratios Of Mixtures can be used to identify columns of the permuted mixing matrix.
the time-frequency ratios of mixtures can provide a very useful information for the identification of sources in mixtures.
AD-TIFROM methods are able to separate mixtures where the sources are not necessarily sparse in time and/or frequency and where the sources are delayed.
